correctness.rationale: All nonzero ideals of the local Gorenstein ring contain the simple socle, which equals m²; the ideals under m are exactly preimages of all k-subspaces of m/m². The multiplication pairing is nondegenerate without a coefficient-field hypothesis, so every a-subspace has a (d−a)-dimensional orthogonal complement and the ordered (a,b) count is exactly a product of Gaussian binomial coefficients. Tuples of nonzero product contain no zero ideal and at most two proper nonzero ideals because m³=0; counting 0/1/2 proper factors proves the exact s-fold formula for every s≥2. A verifier exhausts 12 finite-field configurations and one characteristic-four example; finite checks corroborate but do not replace this proof.

value.rationale: A 2026 primary paper poses nonchain universality of ideal zero-product probability as an open research direction. The theorem supplies a complete all-s formula for all finite short Gorenstein local rings, including nonprincipal, varying embedding dimensions and nonsplit coefficient characteristics. Its dimension-refined incidence and Witt-type blindness versus square-zero-ideal sensitivity give a structural comparison not implied by the chain-ring case.
